agreed — Reports not evidence of truth of contents — Documents used in cross-examination distinguished from witnesses’ resulting concessions — Counsel’s explanation of specialist’s non-attendance not medical evidence — Unproved orthopaedic report not essential to finding — Award of RM3,000 affirmed — No cross-appeal seeking increase DAMAGES — Scarring — Award based on dimensions and locations judgments.title: NG BEE HEAN & ors v LEE POH CHIANG & ors
judgments.catchwords: Final Order Accordingly, it is ordered as follows: (1) Appeal No. WA-12BNCvC-43-04/2026 is allowed in part. The judgment entered in favour of Lee Poh Chiang is varied from RM29,290.36 to RM20,039.70, and the judgment entered in favour of Loke Suet Ling is varied from RM31,510.39 to RM21,894.73. (2) Appeal No. WA-12BNCvC-44-04/2026 is allowed in part. (a) The counterclaim award entered below of RM62,817.60 against Lee Poh Chiang is varied by setting aside so much thereof as relates to the claim for unfinished treatment packages, namely RM53,007.00, leaving an award of RM9,81060, which is affirmed. (b) The counterclaim award entered below of RM97,677.75 against Loke Suet Ling is varied by setting aside so much thereof as relates to the claim for unfinished treatment packages, namely RM50,946.00, leaving an award of RM46,731.75 which is affirmed. The calculation as follows: For P1: Total counterclaim (para 115(c)) — RM62,817.60 Less (unfinished packages) — (RM53,007.00) = RM9,810.60 For P2: Total counterclaim (para 115(c)) — RM97,677.75 Less (unfinished packages) — (RM50,946.00) = RM46,731.75 (3) The set-off applied by the learned Sessions Court Judge, and the net judgments of RM33,527.24 against Lee Poh Chiang and RM66,167.36 against Loke Suet Ling, are set aside. Because each Plaintiff both owes and is owed money, the sums must be set off: • For Lee Poh Chiang, his claim (RM20,039.70) is set off against the counterclaim (RM9,810.60). He remains entitled to a net balance of RM10,229.10, payable by Nutribon Beauty Sanctuary Sdn Bhd. • For Loke Suet Ling, her claim (RM21,894.73) is set off against the counterclaim (RM46,731.75). She remains liable for a net balance of RM24,837.02, payable to Nutribon Beauty Sanctuary Sdn Bhd. (4) Interest at 5% per annum on the sums specified in paragraph (3) shall run from the date of the judgment below until full satisfaction. (5) As to costs: (a) Each party shall bear its own costs of both appeals. (b) The order for costs made by the learned Sessions Court Judge that each party bear its own costs is affirmed.

judgments.title: HAFIZUL BIN HAWARI v Pendakwa Raya
judgments.catchwords: Appeal - against the sentence meted out by the Sessions Court Judge directing the custodial sentences to run consecutively to his existing terms of imprisonment - the sentences should instead have been ordered to take effect from the date of arrest - whether the learned SCJ erred in law and in fact by refusing to direct that the custodial sentences commence from the date of arrest Commencement of a term of imprisonment - statutory default is governed by s. 282(d) of the Criminal Procedure Code which dictates that a sentence takes effect from the date it is passed, unless the court otherwise directs - decision to order an earlier commencement date, such as backdating the sentence to the date of arrest, falls squarely within the judicial discretion of the sentencing judge - backdating of a sentence is not an automatic right - the court is statutorily empowered to direct that a sentence of imprisonment passed on an individual already undergoing a custodial term shall take effect either immediately or upon the expiration of the existing sentence

judgments.catchwords: Offence under section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 read together with section 34 of the Penal Code - Whether the trial judge should have informed at the close of the prosecution's case, that the defence was being called upon to answer a case of actual trafficking or presumed trafficking? - Overwhelming evidence proved the elements of custody, control, and knowledge - Actual possession of the impugned drugs was established - Section 180 (1) and (4) of the Criminal Procedure Code - Procedure after conclusion of case for prosecution - No statutory or legal requirement to state the presumption when calling for the defence - Formal verbal label for an evidentiary rule at the close of the prosecution's case is unnecessary - Statutory presumption of trafficking under section 37(da)(xvi) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 - Section 422 of the Criminal Procedure Code - Not vitiate the conviction - No miscarriage of justice - Failure either to make or to record such a finding does not ipso facto - The law does not require a mini-judgment or detailed legal reasons at the close of the prosecution’s case

judgments.title: BELLWORTH DEVELOPMENTS SDN BHD v SETIAKON BUILDERS SDN BHD
judgments.catchwords: The Court of Appeal reaffirmed the principle of minimal judicial intervention in arbitration. A procedural breach, such as an alleged one-day delay in submitting a draft award for AIAC technical review, does not automatically invalidate an arbitral award where the requirement is merely directory, no timely objection was raised, and no prejudice is shown. An arbitral award will not be set aside on the basis of a purported “new difference” where the issue was within the parties’ pleadings, evidence and submissions. Courts will not review the merits of an award under the guise of a setting-aside application.’
